title: Rational sections and elementary divisor modifications on a regular curve
statement:
Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian regular scheme of dimension one [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-dimension], where Noetherian means quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian, with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field]. For each closed point $x$, let $v_x:K^*\to\mathbf Z$ be the normalized valuation of the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Here $v_x(f)=n$ means $f=u t^n$ for a unit $u\in\mathcal O_{X,x}^*$ and a uniformizer $t$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; $\kappa(x)$ denotes the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Tensor products are those of module sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A divisor means a finite formal sum $D=\sum_xn_x[x]$. Define $\mathcal O_X(D)$ as the subsheaf of the constant rational-function sheaf $K$ whose sections on a nonempty open $U$ are $0$ and the $f\in K^*$ with $v_x(f)+n_x\geq0$ for all closed $x\in U$.
(1) $\mathcal O_X(D)$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], $\mathcal O_X(0)=\mathcal O_X$, and multiplication gives $\mathcal O_X(D)\otimes\mathcal O_X(E)\simeq\mathcal O_X(D+E)$.
(2) If $\mathcal L$ is invertible and $0\ne s\in\mathcal L_\eta$, write $s=f_xe_x$ for a local generator at $x$. The integers $v_x(f_x)$ are independent of that generator and vanish except at finitely many $x$. Put $\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)=\sum_xv_x(f_x)[x]$. Multiplication by $s$ gives $\mathcal O_X(\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s))\simeq\mathcal L$. Such an $s$ always exists. If $s$ is a nonzero global section, its divisor is effective. For $f\in K^*$, $\mathcal O_X(\operatorname{div}(f))\simeq\mathcal O_X$.
(3) For any divisor $D$ and closed point $x$, the natural inclusion fits into a short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal O_X(D-[x])\to\mathcal O_X(D)\to i_{x,*}V\to0$, where $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$, $V$ is a one-dimensional $\kappa(x)$-vector space, viewed as an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module through $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\kappa(x)$, and $i_{x,*}V$ is its skyscraper module at $x$ [def-pc-ringed-module-skyscraper] (sections $V$ on opens containing $x$ and $0$ on the others, i.e. the pushforward of $V$ along $i_x$); hence the last sheaf is noncanonically isomorphic to $i_{x,*}\kappa(x)$.

proof.text: First record the geometry used below. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], $X$ is irreducible. A finite affine cover with Noetherian coordinate rings exists by local Noetherianness and quasi-compactness. Each member has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]; an ascending chain of opens stabilizes on each member, hence stabilizes on their finite union. Thus the underlying space is Noetherian. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] it is sober and $T_0$ (two points with the same closure would both be its unique generic point). By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] its topological dimension is one. Every $y\ne\eta$ is closed: otherwise a proper specialization $z$ of $y$ would give $\overline{\{z\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{y\}}\subsetneq X$, a chain of length two. The generic point is not closed, since otherwise irreducibility would make $X$ a singleton of dimension zero. All nonempty opens contain $\eta$. Consequently [lem-sc-nonempty-open-complement-finite-dim-le-one] applies: every nonempty open has finite complement, consisting of closed points.

source.place: Tag 04MU (lemma-dimension), with Schemes Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober); finite-complement argument as in the cited existing node

proof.text: By [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], identify every $R_y=\mathcal O_{X,y}$ and every ring of sections over a nonempty open with subrings of $K$; $K$ is the fraction field of every $R_y$. For a closed $x$, take an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its generic point is $(0)$ and $x$ corresponds to a nonzero prime $\mathfrak p$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field]. Thus $R_x=A_{\mathfrak p}$ has the strict prime chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}$, so has dimension at least one; it has dimension at most one by the hypothesis defining $\dim X$. It is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme], hence a DVR by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. Choose a uniformizer $t$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] to numerator and denominator of $h\in K^*$ to obtain $h=ut^n$, $u\in R_x^*$, $n\in\mathbf Z$. If $ut^n=u't^{n'}$ and $n<n'$, then $u=u't^{n'-n}$ lies in the maximal ideal, a contradiction; similarly $n>n'$ is impossible with the roles reversed. A second uniformizer differs by a unit, so $n=v_x(h)$ is independent of $t$. Multiplication adds exponents. In particular $v_x(h)\geq0$ exactly when $h\in R_x$, and $v_x(h)=0$ exactly when $h\in R_x^*$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), conditions (3),(4) and unit-times-uniformizer-power assertion; Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves)

proof.text: For later use, each $h\in K^*$ is a unit on some nonempty open. Indeed [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] represents both $h$ and $h^{-1}$ by regular sections on neighbourhoods of $\eta$. Intersect the neighbourhoods. Their product has generic germ $1$, so equals $1$ there by the injectivity in step 2. At every closed point in this open $h$ is a unit, hence $v_x(h)=0$. Step 1 makes the complement finite. Thus the set of closed points with $v_x(h)\ne0$ is finite, without any finite-type-over-a-field or separatedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0078 (section-stalks), description by germs; Divisors Tag 02RL (lemma-divisor-locally-finite), dimension-one quasi-compact case written out

proof.text: The displayed valuation rule in the statement defines a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, with zero module on the empty open. At a closed $x$, the permitted elements are the lattice $t^{-n_x}R_x\subset K$, closed under addition and under scalars from $R_x$ by step 2. For a nonempty open cover of a nonempty $U$, any two nonempty members intersect, since $X$ is irreducible; compatible rational functions on them therefore have the same value in $K$. This common value satisfies the bounds at every point of $U$, proving the sheaf axiom. For $D=0$, every regular function satisfies all bounds by step 2. Conversely a rational function satisfying them belongs to $R_x$ at every closed $x\in U$, and belongs to $R_\eta=K$. By step 1 these are all points of $U$, so [lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue] gives a regular section on $U$ with that rational value. The injectivity from step 2 makes it unique. Thus $\mathcal O_X(0)=\mathcal O_X$ as subsheaves of $K$.

proof.text:
Fix a closed point $x$ and a uniformizer $t\in R_x\subset K$. By step 3 the set of closed $y$ with $v_y(t)
e0$ is finite. Remove all these points other than $x$, and all points of $\operatorname{Supp}D$ other than $x$, obtaining an open $U
i x$. For any nonempty open $V\subseteq U$ and $g\in K^*$, the bounds for $g\in\mathcal O_X(D)(V)$ are equivalent to $v_y(t^{n_x}g)\geq0$ at every closed $y\in V$: at $x$ use $v_x(t)=1$, and at $y
e x$ use $v_y(t)=0=n_y$. Step 4 identifies this condition with $t^{n_x}g\in\mathcal O_X(V)$. Including zero and the empty open gives $\mathcal O_X(D)|_U=t^{-n_x}\mathcal O_U$, compatibly with restrictions. At $\eta$ take $U=X\setminus\operatorname{Supp}D$, where step 4 gives $\mathcal O_X(D)|_U=\mathcal O_U$. These local identifications prove local freeness of rank one, including $(\mathcal O_X(D))_x=t^{-n_x}R_x$. They also prove quasi-coherence: shrink each trivializing open to an affine neighbourhood, where the module is $\widetilde A$. Hence $\mathcal O_X(D)$ is invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module] and [pqf-def-coherent].

proof.text: Multiplication of rational functions satisfies the bounds for $D+E$, since valuations add. It is balanced over $\mathcal O_X$ and respects restrictions, so induces the multiplication morphism on the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. At a closed $x$, use the same $t$ and intersect the trivializing neighbourhoods in step 5 for $D$, $E$ and $D+E$. Multiplication then sends the free generator $t^{-n_x}\otimes t^{-m_x}$ to the free generator $t^{-(n_x+m_x)}$, with inverse on this open sending $a t^{-(n_x+m_x)}$ to $a(t^{-n_x}\otimes t^{-m_x})$. Near $\eta$ it is the identity under the trivializations. These inverses agree on overlaps because each is inverse to the same multiplication map, and therefore glue. This proves $\mathcal O_X(D)\otimes\mathcal O_X(E)\simeq\mathcal O_X(D+E)$.

Let $\mathcal L$ be invertible. A trivialization on a neighbourhood of $\eta$ identifies $\mathcal L_\eta$ with the one-dimensional $K$-vector space $K$ [def-sc-invertible-module], so a nonzero $s$ exists. For any such $s$, a local generator $e$ gives $s=f e_\eta$ with $f\in K^*$. Replacing $e$ by $a e$ for a local unit changes $f$ to $a^{-1}f$, of unchanged valuation at the point in question by step 2. To check finite support, choose a trivializing neighbourhood of $\eta$, write $s=f e_\eta$ there and intersect with a unit neighbourhood for $f$ from step 3. On that nonempty open $s$ is a local generator, so all its valuations vanish. Step 1 gives only finitely many remaining closed points. Thus $D=\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)$ is a well-defined finite divisor.

source.place: Tags 02SF (definition-order-vanishing-meromorphic), 02SG (lemma-divisor-meromorphic-locally-finite) and 0BE6 (definition-divisor-invertible-sheaf); finite support proved from a generic trivialization

proof.text: On a trivializing open $U$ with generator $e$, write $s=f e_\eta$. For every closed $y\in U$, the coefficient of $D=\operatorname{div}_{\mathcal L}(s)$ is $v_y(f)$. Thus, for a nonempty $V\subseteq U$, $g\in\mathcal O_X(D)(V)$ if and only if $gf\in\mathcal O_X(V)$, by step 4. Multiplication by $s$ on $V$ is therefore the map $g\mapsto(gf)e$, with inverse $a e\mapsto a/f$. The maps commute with restrictions and handle the empty open uniquely. On overlaps two such formulas have the same generic germ $gs$. They are equal: locally in a common trivialization equality of coefficients follows from the injectivity of regular sections into $K$ in step 2, and the sheaf axiom then gives equality on the overlap. Thus these maps and their inverses glue to the asserted isomorphism $\mathcal O_X(D)\simeq\mathcal L$.

source.place: Tag 0BE8 (lemma-normal-c1-injective), local trivialization argument, with the actual multiplication isomorphism written explicitly

proof.text: If $s$ is a nonzero global section, its generic germ is nonzero: a section with zero generic germ has zero coefficient on every trivializing open by the injectivity in step 2, hence is zero. Its coefficient in a local generator at a closed $x$ belongs to $R_x$, so step 2 gives $v_x(f_x)\geq0$. Its divisor is therefore effective. Finally apply steps 7 and 8 with $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_X$ and generic section $f\in K^*$: this gives $\mathcal O_X(\operatorname{div}f)\simeq\mathcal O_X$, with isomorphism multiplication by $f$. This checks the sign convention as well.

proof.text: For the last clause fix $x$ and put $M=\mathcal O_X(D)$. The valuation bounds give an inclusion $\mathcal O_X(D-[x])\subseteq M$. Define $V=M_x/\mathfrak m_x M_x$, a vector space over $\kappa(x)=R_x/\mathfrak m_x$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Define $q:M\to i_{x,*}V$ on opens containing $x$ by germ at $x$ followed by this quotient, and by zero on opens not containing $x$. This respects restrictions, and scalars act through $\mathcal O_X(U)\to R_x\to\kappa(x)$. By step 5, $M_x=t^{-n_x}R_x$ and $(\mathcal O_X(D-[x]))_x=t^{1-n_x}R_x=\mathfrak m_xM_x$. Multiplication by $t^{n_x}$ identifies $V$ with $R_x/tR_x=\kappa(x)$, so it is one-dimensional. At $x$ the sequence is exactly the inclusion of this kernel followed by its quotient map. At $y\ne x$, the two divisor modules coincide on $X\setminus\{x\}$ and $(i_{x,*}V)_y=0$: an open neighbourhood avoiding $x$ is available since $x$ is closed. Also $(i_{x,*}V)_x=V$, since by [def-pc-ringed-module-skyscraper] the sections of this skyscraper on every neighbourhood of $x$ are $V$ with identity restrictions. Thus the sequence is short exact at every stalk. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] to the complexes with zero end terms to obtain the claimed sheaf short exact sequence. Choosing a basis of $V$ gives the stated noncanonical isomorphism with $i_{x,*}\kappa(x)$.

Applied only to numerator and denominator in a DVR; uniqueness and valuation properties are calculated in the step.

Every hypothesis of the finite-complement node is checked. (2) An affine chart is a domain with x↔p≠0, so 1≤dim≤1, regular, hence a DVR. (4) The gluing works because nonempty opens of an irreducible space meet, and O(0)=O_X follows from the gluing node over closed points and η. (5) O(D)|_U=t^{-n_x}O_U, with the bound equivalence checked at x and at y≠x; quasi-coherence holds on affine shrinkings. (6) The multiplication is a local isomorphism of the sheafified tensor. (10) The stalk of O(D-[x]) at x is m_x M_x, V≅κ(x), and stalkwise exactness applies. Edge cases tested: D=0, D=-[x] (tR/t^2R), the spectrum of a DVR, a non-separated doubled-point curve, the empty open.
